Folks — quick legal/ops note to tighten sequencing and reduce blocking risk.

On Thu, Aug 12, 2026 at 12:22 PM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai> wrote:
> - Week 1 (Aug 16–20): Redwood sends MSA baseline + redline guidance to Crescent legal (small team review).

Proposal from legal:
- Formal approach: Issue MSA baseline + a 'negotiation playbook' that calls out non-negotiables (data residency, indemnity caps, export controls) and a short list of negotiable items. That reduces oscillation.
- DPA: run the DPA questionnaire in parallel with a highlighted exception log. Provide a template clause for subprocessor updates to avoid full contract amendment later.
- Order Form: do not finalize commercial terms until MSA has a versioned sign-off token (we can use a simple \"MSA v1.0 signed\" flag in the DocuSign envelope).

Suggested sequencing (concrete):
1) Aug 16: Redwood sends MSA v1 + negotiation playbook.
2) Aug 17–20: Crescent legal returns consolidated comments.
3) Aug 23: Redwood responds with MSA v1.1 (highlighted).
4) Aug 24–27: DPA finalization and security checklist (SOC2 evidence link confirmed).
5) Aug 30: Order Form drafted; finance check.
6) Sep 2: DocuSign prepared and routing tested; Sep 3: target signature.

If Crescent requires substantive changes to indemnity/limitations, trigger exec escalation channel and a parallel pricing hold.

—Karthik
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
